answer: For each prelisted mapping task in an atlas, validators auction one indivisible compute slot. Sealed prepaid bids close together; the highest pays its own price, losers receive refunds, and ties use earliest confirmed bid. A terrace survey offers no account bonus. With 100 coins, 100 aliases cannot outbid one 100-coin bid; another slot requires another winning payment. More names surveying a knoll create no slots. This limits access farming, not fake names; task curators are trusted and wealth can dominate.
